components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p16.measurable-ci-calculus) is not supplied for the statement's clause 'Measurable functions may be applied to either independent tuple, also using the conditioning tuple as an argument' (body 47-48). Its only argument is annex 53-56, 'by pushing forward the conditional product kernels at each z', a sketch: no step shows that the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) given Z=z is the image of the conditional product law at z under (x,y)->(g(x,z),h(y,z)) (the substitution identity of thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure is neither used nor cited), and none returns from that kernel identity to the product-test definition. The Z-free case (composing bounded tests), both equivalences and the four semigraphoid properties are argued in full.

components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p16.measurable-kernel-randomization) is not supplied for the 'Consequently' assertion (body 90-94) that every finite standard Borel kernel model has a representation X_v=F_v(X_pa(v),U_v) with mutually independent uniform U_v. Annex 157-160 says only 'Topological evaluation and successive conditioning show that its joint law is the kernel law': it does not establish that each U_v is independent of the already constructed predecessors, that the realization property then makes K_v(X_pa(v),.) their conditional law, or the inductive identification of the joint law with P_K through thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure; the later argument at annex 508-513 is not invoked. The single-kernel jointly measurable realization (annex 112-155) and the non-uniqueness example (160-166) are complete.

components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p16.measurable-response-component) is not supplied for the stated consequence (body 304-307) that one conditional product law of (R,B) given C licenses integration of the whole family at a measurable random parameter depending on (B,C). Annex 567-573 is a two-sentence sketch ('its conditional joint law with R is the corresponding pushforward of this product kernel ... Integrating the jointly measurable F against that joint law proves the stated random-substitution license'): it does not derive L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels from R independent of B given C, nor the substitution of the random parameter into F via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure. In addition annex 537-538 ('It contains no vertex of B, by the separation hypothesis') uses, unstated and uncited, that exposing private roots preserves d-separation (stated only later, annex 580-581, in another proof) and the moral-separation bridge. The pointwise representation Y^t=F(t,C,R) (545-555) and R independent of B given C (557-565) are argued.

components.gap: The full treatment promised by the declared status (proved=annex:p16.measurable-mediation-fields) is not supplied for item 1 (body 364-365). In the cross-world field the identity 'The mediator tuple in this auxiliary model is exactly M_b, by topological evaluation on its restored ancestors' (annex 610-611) requires every exposure child that is an ancestor of a mediator to lie outside D_Y, so that its exposure input is b rather than a (annex 607-608 assigns a to every exposure child in D_Y). The 'exact graph facts' listed at annex 594-605 place in D_M only the heads of restored mediator edges and their remaining parents; no step places the other exposure children among the mediator ancestors in D_M, so the claimed construction of M_b, and hence R_0 independent of M_b given C for each b, is not fully argued. The companion claim that every vertex needed for Y belongs to D_Y (613-615) is also only asserted. Items 2 and 3 (628-816), the reference-mediator law (818-828) and the common-measure reading are argued.

'This is the source's kernel-combination argument with the needed product/Fubini domains made explicit.' The held Lauritzen Proposition 2.46 proof (p. 66) is an induction on a terminal vertex that swaps only the last two vertices via Proposition 2.17; the handbook's argument connects arbitrary topological orders by adjacent swaps at any position. The common tool is commutativity of kernel combination, but the sentence presents a different argument as the source's.

History-based stochastic interventions use 'a specified probability kernel on earlier coordinates', but 'earlier' is not tied to a stated order. If it meant a topological order of G the separately imposed acyclicity requirement would be automatic; the intended order is left implicit.

For history-based replacements 'the same argument gives its kernel law and global Markov property', but the preceding argument proves only the kernel law; the global Markov conclusion needs thm:p16-measurable-global-markov, which is not cited. 'The kernel section theorem' (lines 506-507) is named without a label.

The warning asserts that each structural output kernel of the projected model is the constant mass function (1/2,1/2) without the one-line computation from q(z,a,b)=alpha(a)alpha(b)/2 (z fair and independent of a and b). The value is checkable directly from the stated model; recorded, not counted as a gap.

def:p16-measurable-dag-kernels uses 'a finite DAG' and then treats 'the empty graph', while def:p16-causal-dag (finite-causal-models.tex line 24) defines a finite DAG only for n>=1. The empty-graph boundary is handled in the measurable proofs, but the governing definition of a finite DAG excludes it.
